diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the noise-free case \eqref{constrain_model}, we assume that any $(n-1)$-column submatrix of $A$ has full row rank.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs a single null vector of A that is nonzero on every coordinate of the boundary set $\cI_0$; this is asserted without any argument. It does follow from the rank hypothesis (any $m$ columns of $A$ are independent, so each coordinate functional is nonzero on $\ker A$, and a real vector space is not a finite union of the proper subspaces $\{v_i=0\}$), but the paper supplies none of this. Separately, when every component satisfies $|\hat x_i|=\mu$ (so $\cI_1\cup\cI_2=\emptyset$), the quantity $\rho$ is a minimum over the empty set and is undefined, so the proof does not cover this case even though the conclusion still holds by a direct perturbation. The theorem's conclusion is correct; the proof has these two gaps.

failure_location.quote: Since $\cI_0 \neq \emptyset$, construct $\vv \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $A\vv = \mathbf{0}$, $\|\vv\|_2 = 1$, and $\vv_i \neq 0$ for $i \in \cI_0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the short spark-based argument that $\ker A$ contains a vector nonzero on all of $\cI_0$ (each coordinate functional is nonzero on $\ker A$, and $\ker A$ is not contained in the finite union of the coordinate hyperplanes), and handle the case $\cI_1\cup\cI_2=\emptyset$ separately (any such full-support null vector gives a strict decrease of $\Phi_\mu(\hat x-\epsilon v)$).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem THdifferentiable_refined lacks a complete proof as written; downstream results that only cite its (correct) conclusion, such as the necessity direction of linearoptcond, remain valid once the proof is patched.
issues.title: Differentiability proof: unjustified null-vector construction and an unhandled degenerate case
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is correct and both repairs are short, local additions that preserve the method, conclusion, and advertised scope; no rate or guarantee is lost.

A vector $\widehat{\vx}$ minimizes \eqref{constrain_model} locally or globally if and only if $\abs{\wvx_i}\neq \mu$ for all $i$ and there exists $\wvy\in\rr^m$ such that
At the limit point, the following hold:

issues.failure_explanation: The proofs pass to a limit of the BCD sequence and apply Theorems linearoptcond/noise_optcond, whose hypotheses require $|\hat x_i|\neq\mu$ for all $i$; since $\cH_\mu$ is discontinuous at $|x_i|=\mu$, the limit of the binary filter sequence need not satisfy this, so the assertion that the limit obeys $\hat\omega=\cH_\mu(\hat x)$ and is a minimizer is unjustified. The failure is not merely a gap: the statements are false. Noise-free counterexample: $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $b=(2\mu,\mu)$ has spark $3=m+1$; with feasible $x^0=(\mu,\mu,0)$ (which equals the paper's $L_1$-min-norm initialization) and $\omega^0=\cH_\mu(x^0)=(0,0,0)$, $\cQ_\mu(x^0,\omega^0)=2<3$, the BCD $x$-update returns the min-norm solution $x^1=A^\top(AA^\top)^{-1}b=(\mu,\mu,0)=x^0$, so the algorithm stops immediately at $(\mu,\mu,0)$; but the feasible point $(1.1\mu,0.9\mu,-0.1\mu)$ has $\Phi_\mu=1+0.81+0.01=1.82<2=\Phi_\mu(\mu,\mu,0)$, so the limit is not a local minimizer. Noisy counterexample: same $A$ with $\mu=1$, $\alpha=4$, $b=(2.5,1)$; $\bar x=(1,1,0)$ uniquely minimizes $\cJ_\mu(\cdot,(0,0,0))$ (KKT holds: $4A^\top(A\bar x-b)+2\bar x=0$), $\cJ_\mu(\bar x,(0,0,0))=2.5<3=\mathrm{spark}(A)$, yet $\cG_\mu(1+\epsilon,1+\epsilon,0)=2.5-4\epsilon+10\epsilon^2<2.5$ for $0<\epsilon<0.4$, so $\bar x$ is not a local minimizer.

failure_location.quote: Then, the sequence $\{(\wvx^{k},\widehat{\vomega}^{k})\}_k$ is bounded and converges to the minimizer of model \eqref{constrain_model} in a finite number of steps.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either (i) impose and verify a non-degeneracy condition excluding BCD fixed points with some $|\hat x_i|=\mu$ (a condition on $(\mu,b)$ and/or the initialization that is preserved by the iteration), or (ii) weaken the conclusion to finite convergence to a KKT point/fixed point of the BCD map rather than to a minimizer, or (iii) modify the algorithm (e.g., deterministic tie-breaking of $\cH_\mu$ at $|x_i|=\mu$, or a perturbation scheme) together with a new convergence analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's headline guarantee (abstract, introduction, conclusions: finite-step convergence to a minimizer under spark conditions) is false under the stated hypotheses; both convergence theorems are invalidated, and the BCD algorithm may terminate at a point that is not a local minimizer, including from the paper's own $L_1$-min-norm initialization.
issues.title: Finite-step convergence theorems are false: BCD can stall at a non-minimizer on the non-differentiability set $\{|x_i|=\mu\}$
issues.why_classification: A central advertised guarantee is false with explicit counterexamples satisfying all stated hypotheses (including the paper's own initialization); every repair either changes the guarantee type (fixed point instead of minimizer), excludes an advertised regime, or requires a new algorithmic construction and analysis, so no comparable version of the primary claim survives as stated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: From Lemma \ref{mudecre_objincre} and Lemma \ref{upperbound_lema2_rev}, we can easily obtain

where 
$\mathcal{K}+1=\{i\mid \abs{(\wvx_{k})_i}\leq c_{k+1}\}$, $c_{k+1}=\tfrac{\mu_{k}}{\rho}$, and $\rho>1$ is a constant.
\STATE Compute $(\wvx_k, \widehat{\vomega}_k)$ by applying steps 2–7 of Algorithm \ref{BCD}, using $(\wvx_{k-1}, \widehat{\vomega}_{k-1}, \mu_k)$ as the initialization

issues.failure_explanation: The update is presented as a consequence of Lemma mudecre_objincre (monotonicity of the optimal value in $\mu$) and Lemma upperbound_lema2_rev (the surrogate identity), neither of which implies it. Its denominator $m-n+\mathrm{card}(\mathcal K+1)$ is nonpositive whenever at most $n-m$ components of $x_k$ lie below $c_{k+1}$, so $\mu_{k+1}$ is undefined (division by zero or square root of a negative number) in that regime. The outer loop also references $(x_{k-1},\omega_{k-1})$ at $k=0$, which is undefined. The continuation strategy is a heuristic add-on (the convergence theorems are for fixed $\mu$), so the defect is local to this procedure.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Guard the update (require $\mathrm{card}(\mathcal K+1)>n-m$ and otherwise keep $\mu_{k+1}=\mu_k$ or use a safe fallback), present the rule as a heuristic choice rather than a consequence of the two lemmas, and fix the $k=0$ initialization reference.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm continuescheme may fail to produce a valid $\mu_{k+1}$ when few components of the current iterate are small; its claimed invertibility preservation rests on an unsupported and sometimes undefined update.
issues.title: Continuation update rule can be undefined, is not derived from the cited lemmas, and has an off-by-one initialization
issues.why_classification: Short local guards and a wording correction repair the procedure; the fixed-$\mu$ convergence theory and the experiments are unaffected.
